questions.stem: Reading from the bottom line upwards, the notes on the five lines of the treble staff are
questions.explanation: Treble lines are E G B D F; F A C E are the treble spaces and G B D F A are the bass lines.

questions.stem: In the alto (C) clef, middle C is written on the
questions.explanation: The C clef marks middle C; in the alto position it is centred on the third line (in the tenor position it is on the fourth line).

questions.stem: The pattern of tones (T) and semitones (S) in a major scale is
options: T S T T S T T
T T T S T T S
S T T T S T T
T T S T T T S
questions.explanation: Every major scale follows T T S T T T S; T S T T S T T is the natural minor.

questions.stem: The note that is raised in the harmonic minor scale of A is
questions.explanation: The harmonic minor raises the 7th degree: in A minor G becomes G#.

questions.stem: In the ascending form of the melodic minor scale of A, the sixth and seventh notes are
questions.explanation: The melodic minor raises both 6th and 7th ascending (F#, G#) and lowers them descending.

questions.stem: A five-note mode such as d r m s l is called a
questions.explanation: Penta = five; hexatonic has six and heptatonic seven notes.

questions.stem: The pentatonic mode d r m s l omits which two notes of the major scale?
questions.explanation: This anhemitonic pentatonic leaves out fah and te, so it has no semitones.

questions.stem: The key signature of E major has
questions.explanation: E major: F#, C#, G#, D#.

questions.stem: The relative minor of E flat major is
questions.explanation: The relative minor starts on the 6th degree of the major scale: C, sharing three flats.

questions.stem: A key signature of four flats belongs to
options: E flat major or C minor
D flat major or B flat minor
E major or C sharp minor
A flat major or F minor
questions.explanation: Four flats (Bb, Eb, Ab, Db) = A flat major and its relative F minor.

questions.stem: The order in which sharps are written in a key signature is
options: B E A D G C F
C G D A E B F
F C G D A E B
F G C D A B E
questions.explanation: Sharps follow F C G D A E B; flats run the reverse, B E A D G C F.

questions.stem: A time signature of 3/4 is described as
questions.explanation: Three crotchet beats per bar, each divisible into two quavers: simple triple.

questions.stem: Which time signature indicates compound duple time?
questions.explanation: 6/8 has two dotted-crotchet beats per bar; 9/8 is compound triple.

questions.stem: How many semiquavers make up one complete bar of 9/8?
questions.explanation: 9 quavers per bar, each equal to 2 semiquavers: 18.

questions.stem: The basic beat (pulse) in 12/8 time is the
options: dotted minim, two to a bar
dotted crotchet, four to a bar
questions.explanation: 12/8 is compound quadruple: four dotted-crotchet beats, each of three quavers.

questions.stem: The interval from C up to G is a
questions.explanation: C-G spans five letter names and seven semitones: a perfect fifth.

questions.stem: The interval from C up to A is a
questions.explanation: C D E F G A: six letters, nine semitones = major 6th.

questions.stem: The interval from F up to B (both natural) is
questions.explanation: F-B is a fourth by letter but six semitones: augmented fourth (the tritone).

questions.stem: When a major third is inverted, it becomes a
questions.explanation: Inverted numbers add to 9 and major becomes minor: major 3rd -> minor 6th.

questions.stem: In the key of D major, the tonic sol-fa note "soh" is
questions.explanation: Doh = D, so ray E, me F#, fah G, soh A.

questions.stem: In F major, the note E is sung to the sol-fa syllable
questions.explanation: F major: d F, r G, m A, f Bb, s C, l D, t E.

questions.stem: A clarinet in B flat sounds
options: a major second higher than written
a perfect fifth lower than written
a major second lower than written
questions.explanation: B flat instruments sound a tone below written pitch, so parts are written a tone higher.

questions.stem: A concert-pitch melody in F major is to be written for a B flat trumpet. The trumpet part should be written in
questions.explanation: Write a major second higher: F major becomes G major.

questions.topic: Musical terms, signs, ornaments and abbreviations
questions.stem: The Italian term "andante" means
questions.explanation: Andante = moderately slow, walking pace.

questions.topic: Musical terms, signs, ornaments and abbreviations
questions.stem: The sign "pp" (pianissimo) instructs the performer to play
questions.explanation: pp = very soft; ff = very loud.

questions.topic: Musical terms, signs, ornaments and abbreviations
questions.stem: "Rallentando" (rall.) means
questions.explanation: Rallentando slows gradually; accelerando speeds up.

questions.topic: Musical terms, signs, ornaments and abbreviations
questions.stem: A rapid alternation between a written note and the note above it is the ornament called
questions.explanation: A trill alternates rapidly with the upper neighbour; a mordent is a single quick alternation.

questions.topic: Musical terms, signs, ornaments and abbreviations
questions.stem: The abbreviation "D.C. al Fine" directs the performer to
options: go back to the sign and play to the coda
go back to the beginning and play until the word Fine
play the passage an octave higher
questions.explanation: Da capo = from the head (beginning); al Fine = to the end marked Fine.

questions.stem: The notes of the tonic triad of D major are
questions.explanation: Tonic triad = degrees 1, 3, 5 of D major: D F# A.

questions.stem: In C major, the chord D-F-A is chord
questions.explanation: D is the 2nd degree of C major; D-F-A is the minor supertonic triad.

questions.stem: A triad with its third in the bass is said to be in
questions.explanation: Third in bass = first inversion (6/3); fifth in bass = second inversion (6/4).

questions.stem: In any major key, the chord built on the leading note (vii) is
questions.explanation: For example B-D-F in C major: minor third + diminished fifth = diminished triad.

questions.stem: The dominant seventh chord of G major consists of
options: D, F sharp, A, C sharp
questions.explanation: V of G is D-F#-A; adding the minor 7th above D gives C.

questions.stem: A cadence formed by chord V moving to chord I is the
questions.explanation: V-I is the perfect (authentic) cadence.

questions.stem: The "Amen" sung at the end of many hymns usually forms a
questions.explanation: IV-I is the plagal or "Amen" cadence.

questions.stem: Any cadence that ends on the dominant chord is called
questions.explanation: Imperfect (half) cadences end on V, e.g. I-V, ii-V, IV-V.

questions.stem: In F major, a progression from C-E-G to D-F-A at a cadence is
questions.explanation: In F major C-E-G is V and D-F-A is vi; V-vi is the interrupted cadence.

questions.stem: A non-chord note that moves by step between two different chord notes is a
questions.explanation: A passing note fills the gap between two chord notes by step.

questions.stem: A piece in G major modulates to its dominant key. The new key is
questions.explanation: The dominant of G is D; D major adds C sharp.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT closely related to C major?
questions.explanation: Closely related keys differ by at most one accidental: G, F, A minor (and D minor, E minor). E major has four sharps.

questions.stem: In four-part harmony (SATB), the voice written immediately above the bass is the
questions.explanation: From lowest: bass, tenor, alto, soprano.

questions.stem: In four-part writing, which of the following is regarded as a fault?
options: Contrary motion between soprano and bass
Consecutive perfect fifths between two parts
Doubling the root of a root-position chord
Keeping common notes in the same part
questions.explanation: Parallel (consecutive) fifths and octaves weaken part independence and are avoided.

questions.stem: In two-part counterpoint, the motion in which one part rises while the other falls is
questions.explanation: Contrary motion keeps parts independent; oblique has one part stationary.

questions.stem: When continuing a given opening phrase into a 16-bar melody, the final phrase should normally end on the
options: tonic, with a perfect cadence feel
questions.explanation: Ending on the tonic gives a sense of finality to the melody.

questions.stem: In setting English words to music, stressed syllables should normally fall on
options: the last quaver of every bar
questions.explanation: Matching verbal stress to metrical stress keeps the words natural.

questions.stem: A piece in which the first section returns after a contrasting middle section (A B A) is in
questions.explanation: ABA is ternary; AB is binary.

questions.stem: The pattern A B A C A is typical of
questions.explanation: A recurring main theme alternating with episodes is rondo.

questions.stem: A song in which every verse is sung to the same music is described as
questions.explanation: Strophic songs repeat the same tune for each verse; through-composed songs have new music throughout.

questions.stem: A large musical work for soloist and orchestra, usually in three movements, is a
questions.explanation: The concerto contrasts a soloist with the orchestra, commonly in three movements.

questions.stem: The main difference between an opera and an oratorio is that an oratorio
options: is performed without costumes, scenery or acting
questions.explanation: Both use soloists, chorus and orchestra, but an oratorio is not staged.

questions.stem: The three main sections of sonata form are
questions.explanation: Sonata form presents themes, develops them, then restates them.

questions.stem: A song pattern in which a lead singer sings a line and a chorus answers is
questions.explanation: Call and response (antiphony) is basic to African vocal music.

questions.stem: Repetition of a short rhythmic or melodic pattern over and over in African music produces
questions.explanation: Ostinato-based repetition creates cyclic form.

questions.topic: Form in contemporary African art music
questions.stem: Nigerian art composers often create an African idiom in written music by
options: using indigenous melodies, speech-tone patterns and drum rhythms within Western forms
writing only for European orchestras without African instruments
questions.explanation: Composers draw on folk tunes, tonal inflection of language and traditional rhythms.

questions.stem: In a rhythmic dictation test, candidates are expected to write the rhythm of the melody
questions.explanation: Rhythmic dictation records durations only, written on one pitch.

questions.stem: In the practical examination, playing an unfamiliar short piece at first sight is known as
questions.explanation: Sight-reading tests the ability to perform unseen music.

questions.explanation: Haruna Ishola was a famous Yoruba apala musician.

questions.explanation: Fela created Afrobeat from highlife, jazz, funk and Yoruba rhythms.

questions.stem: Sikiru Ayinde Barrister is credited with popularising
questions.explanation: Barrister developed fuji from Islamic were/ajisari music.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Music: Nigerian Popular Musicians
questions.stem: Which of the following musicians is a juju artiste?
questions.explanation: Sunny Ade is a juju musician; Majek Fashek reggae, Salawa Abeni waka, Olaiya highlife.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Music: Contemporary Nigerian Art Musicians
questions.stem: Fela Sowande is best known as a
options: composer and organist of Nigerian art music
questions.explanation: Sowande composed works such as the African Suite and was a noted organist.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Music: Contemporary Nigerian Art Musicians
questions.stem: Akin Euba is associated with the idea of "African pianism", which means
options: banning the piano from African music
writing piano music based on African rhythmic and melodic practices
using the piano only to accompany hymns
questions.explanation: Euba promoted piano writing drawing on African drumming and melodic techniques.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Music: Contemporary Nigerian Art Musicians
questions.stem: Ikoli Harcourt-Whyte is best remembered for his
options: choral compositions in the Igbo language
questions.explanation: Harcourt-Whyte wrote many Igbo choral and church works.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Western Music
questions.stem: Johann Sebastian Bach belongs to the
questions.explanation: Bach (1685-1750) is a leading Baroque composer.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Western Music
questions.stem: The oratorio "Messiah" was composed by
questions.explanation: Handel composed Messiah in 1741.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Western Music
questions.stem: Which composer wrote nine symphonies and continued composing after becoming deaf?
questions.explanation: Beethoven composed his Ninth Symphony while profoundly deaf.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Western Music
questions.stem: The twelve-tone (serial) method of composition was developed by
questions.explanation: Schoenberg devised the twelve-tone technique in the early 1920s.

questions.stem: Bob Marley is famous for which style of music?
questions.explanation: Bob Marley of Jamaica popularised reggae worldwide.

questions.stem: Scott Joplin, composer of "Maple Leaf Rag", is associated with
questions.explanation: Joplin was the leading ragtime composer.

questions.stem: The Mighty Sparrow and Lord Kitchener are famous exponents of
questions.explanation: Both were celebrated Trinidadian calypsonians.

questions.topic: Role of music in traditional African society
questions.stem: A song sung to soothe a baby to sleep is a
questions.explanation: Lullabies calm children; dirges are sung for the dead.

questions.stem: In the classification of musical instruments, drums with skin heads are
questions.explanation: Membranophones sound by a stretched membrane.

questions.stem: The shekere (gourd rattle covered with a net of beads) is classified as
questions.explanation: The body of the instrument itself vibrates when shaken: idiophone.

questions.stem: The goje, a bowed instrument played among the Hausa and Yoruba, belongs to the class of
questions.explanation: The goje is a bowed fiddle with a string: chordophone.

questions.stem: The simultaneous use of several different rhythms in an ensemble is called
questions.explanation: Polyrhythm layers different rhythmic patterns at the same time.

questions.stem: A song sung to mourn a dead person is a
questions.explanation: Dirges are funeral laments.

questions.topic: Relationship of music to other arts
questions.stem: In traditional African festivals, music is closely linked with dance because
options: drum rhythms direct the steps and movements of the dancers
music is performed only after the dance has ended
questions.explanation: Drummers signal changes and dancers respond to rhythmic cues.

questions.stem: Atilogwu, a lively acrobatic dance, is performed mainly by the
questions.explanation: Atilogwu is an energetic Igbo acrobatic dance.

questions.stem: Swange is a popular traditional dance of the
questions.explanation: Swange is a Tiv dance from Benue.

questions.stem:
(a) Write out, using letter names, the ascending scale of E flat major and name its key signature. [5 marks]
(b) Write out, using letter names, the ascending harmonic minor scale of D and state the note that has been altered. [5 marks]
(c) Name the relative minor of A major and state its key signature. [4 marks]
(d) Explain the difference between the harmonic and melodic forms of the minor scale. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: E flat F G A flat B flat C D E flat (all correct)
2 marks: Key signature: three flats, B flat, E flat, A flat
3 marks: D E F G A B flat C sharp D (all correct)
2 marks: Altered note: 7th degree raised, C becomes C sharp
2 marks: Relative minor of A major: F sharp minor
2 marks: Key signature: three sharps, F sharp, C sharp, G sharp
3 marks: Harmonic minor raises the 7th degree both ascending and descending, giving an augmented 2nd between 6th and 7th
3 marks: Melodic minor raises 6th and 7th ascending and restores (lowers) them descending (natural minor)
questions.explanation: Eb major: Eb F G Ab Bb C D Eb (3 flats). D harmonic minor: D E F G A Bb C# D (7th raised). Relative minor of A major is F# minor (3 sharps). Harmonic raises 7 both ways; melodic raises 6 and 7 ascending only.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the following intervals (the second note is above the first): (i) D to F; (ii) C to G sharp; (iii) G to F; (iv) B flat to D; (v) D to C sharp. [10 marks]
(b) What is meant by the inversion of an interval? [2 marks]
(c) Invert each of the following and name the result: (i) major third; (ii) perfect fourth; (iii) minor seventh; (iv) augmented fourth. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: D to F: minor 3rd
2 marks: C to G sharp: augmented 5th
2 marks: G to F: minor 7th
2 marks: B flat to D: major 3rd
2 marks: D to C sharp: major 7th
2 marks: Inversion: the lower note is placed an octave higher (or the upper an octave lower); numbers add up to nine
2 marks: Major 3rd inverts to minor 6th
2 marks: Perfect 4th inverts to perfect 5th
2 marks: Minor 7th inverts to major 2nd
2 marks: Augmented 4th inverts to diminished 5th
questions.explanation: m3, aug 5, m7, M3, M7. Inversion moves one note by an octave; the numbers sum to 9, major<->minor, augmented<->diminished, perfect stays perfect: M3->m6, P4->P5, m7->M2, aug4->dim5.

questions.stem:
A melody at concert pitch in F major uses the notes F, G, A, B flat, C, A, F.
(a) Explain what is meant by a transposing instrument. [3 marks]
(b) Transpose the melody for a clarinet in B flat so that it sounds at the given pitch, naming the new key and writing the notes in letter names. [9 marks]
(c) State the interval of transposition for: (i) horn in F; (ii) alto saxophone in E flat. [4 marks]
(d) Give two reasons why music is transposed. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Transposing instrument: one whose written notes sound at a different pitch from that written
2 marks: B flat clarinet sounds a major 2nd lower, so the part is written a major 2nd higher
2 marks: New key: G major (one sharp)
5 marks: Notes: G, A, B, C, D, B, G (all correct = 5; deduct 1 per error)
2 marks: Horn in F: written a perfect 5th higher than it sounds
2 marks: Alto saxophone in E flat: written a major 6th higher than it sounds
4 marks: Any two (2 each): to suit the range of a voice or instrument; for transposing instruments; to make a piece easier to read/play; to change the mood/colour of a piece
questions.explanation: A B flat clarinet sounds a tone lower than written, so the melody is written a tone higher: G A B C D B G in G major. Horn in F: written a perfect 5th up; E flat alto sax: a major 6th up. Transposition suits voices, instruments and readability.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the primary triads of D major, giving the notes of each. [6 marks]
(b) Describe the following cadences, stating the chords used: (i) perfect; (ii) plagal; (iii) imperfect; (iv) interrupted. [8 marks]
(c) In D major, name the chords (by notes) that would form a perfect cadence and an interrupted cadence. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: I (tonic): D F sharp A
2 marks: IV (subdominant): G B D
2 marks: V (dominant): A C sharp E
2 marks: Perfect: V-I, sounds final/complete
2 marks: Plagal: IV-I, the "Amen" cadence
2 marks: Imperfect: ends on V (e.g. I-V, ii-V, IV-V), sounds incomplete
2 marks: Interrupted: V-vi, unexpected ending
3 marks: Perfect cadence in D: A C sharp E to D F sharp A
3 marks: Interrupted cadence in D: A C sharp E to B D F sharp
questions.explanation: D major primaries: D-F#-A, G-B-D, A-C#-E. Perfect V-I, plagal IV-I, imperfect ends on V, interrupted V-vi. In D: perfect A-C#-E -> D-F#-A; interrupted A-C#-E -> B-D-F#.

questions.stem:
(a) State six principles a composer should follow when setting an English text to music. [12 marks]
(b) Explain the following terms as used in vocal writing: (i) syllabic setting; (ii) melismatic setting. [4 marks]
(c) Why should the range of a melody written for a school choir be limited? [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
12 marks: Any six principles (2 each): stressed syllables on strong beats; follow the natural rhythm of speech; melody should reflect the mood/meaning of the words; phrases should match the lines/punctuation of the text; avoid awkward leaps on unstressed or short syllables; keep within the range of the voice; cadences at ends of lines/sentences; important words given longer or higher notes; choose a suitable key and time signature
2 marks: Syllabic: one note to each syllable
2 marks: Melismatic: several notes sung on one syllable
4 marks: Range limited because untrained young voices have a narrow comfortable range; extreme notes strain the voice and cause poor intonation (2 points x 2)
questions.explanation: Good word setting matches verbal stress to strong beats, follows speech rhythm and punctuation, reflects meaning, and stays in a singable range. Syllabic = one note per syllable; melismatic = many notes per syllable.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between an opera and an oratorio. [6 marks]
(b) Name one composer of opera and one composer of oratorio, with one work by each. [4 marks]
(c) Describe the structure of sonata form. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Opera: a drama set to music and staged with costumes, scenery and acting; usually secular
3 marks: Oratorio: large work for soloists, chorus and orchestra, usually on a sacred subject, performed without staging or costumes
2 marks: Opera composer and work, e.g. Mozart: The Magic Flute / Monteverdi: Orfeo / Wagner
2 marks: Oratorio composer and work, e.g. Handel: Messiah / Haydn: The Creation / Mendelssohn: Elijah
4 marks: Exposition: first subject in tonic, transition, second subject in dominant (or relative major), codetta
3 marks: Development: themes broken up and developed, passing through various keys
3 marks: Recapitulation: both subjects restated in the tonic, often followed by a coda
questions.explanation: Opera is staged drama in music; oratorio is unstaged and usually sacred. Mozart's Magic Flute; Handel's Messiah. Sonata form: exposition (two subjects in contrasting keys), development, recapitulation in the tonic, coda.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Western Music
questions.stem:
(a) Give the approximate dates of the Baroque period in music. [2 marks]
(b) State six characteristics of Baroque music. [6 marks]
(c) Write on Johann Sebastian Bach under the following headings: (i) nationality and dates; (ii) instrument for which he was famous; (iii) two of his works. [8 marks]
(d) Name two other Baroque composers. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: About 1600 to 1750
6 marks: Any six (1 each): basso continuo/figured bass; terraced dynamics; ornamentation; contrapuntal texture (fugue); motor rhythms; single mood (affection) per movement; major-minor tonality established; rise of opera, oratorio, concerto grosso, suite
2 marks: German, 1685-1750
2 marks: Organ (also harpsichord); church musician at Leipzig
4 marks: Any two works (2 each): Brandenburg Concertos; St Matthew Passion; Mass in B minor; The Well-Tempered Clavier
4 marks: Any two (2 each): Handel, Vivaldi, Purcell, Corelli, Monteverdi, Domenico Scarlatti
questions.explanation: Baroque c. 1600-1750: continuo, counterpoint, terraced dynamics, ornamentation. Bach (German, 1685-1750), organist, wrote the Brandenburg Concertos and Well-Tempered Clavier. Others: Handel, Vivaldi, Purcell.

questions.topic: History and Literature of Music: Nigerian Popular Musicians
questions.stem:
(a) Write on Fela Anikulapo Kuti under the following headings: (i) the style of music he pioneered; (ii) instruments used in his band; (iii) themes of his songs. [12 marks]
(b) Name one musician each associated with: (i) highlife; (ii) juju; (iii) fuji; (iv) Afro-reggae. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Style: Afrobeat, a fusion of highlife, jazz, funk and Yoruba traditional rhythms with long instrumental sections and call and response
4 marks: Instruments (any four, 1 each): saxophones, trumpets, electric guitars, bass guitar, keyboards/organ, drum set, conga/percussion, shekere, clips/sticks
4 marks: Themes (any two, 2 each): social and political criticism; corruption; human rights; African pride/identity; colonial mentality
2 marks: Highlife: e.g. Victor Olaiya, Rex Lawson, Osita Osadebe, Victor Uwaifo, Bobby Benson
2 marks: Juju: e.g. I. K. Dairo, Ebenezer Obey, King Sunny Ade, Shina Peters
2 marks: Fuji: e.g. Sikiru Ayinde Barrister, Ayinla Kollington, Wasiu Ayinde Marshall
2 marks: Afro-reggae: e.g. Majek Fashek, Ras Kimono, Evi Edna Ogholi
questions.explanation: Fela pioneered Afrobeat, blending highlife, jazz, funk and Yoruba rhythms with a big horn section, guitars, keyboards and percussion; his lyrics criticised corruption and oppression. Highlife: Victor Olaiya; juju: Sunny Ade; fuji: Barrister; reggae: Majek Fashek.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the four main classes of musical instruments and explain how each produces sound. [8 marks]
(b) Give one Nigerian traditional instrument as an example of each class. [4 marks]
(c) State four non-musical functions of traditional musical instruments. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Idiophones: the body of the instrument vibrates (struck, shaken, scraped)
2 marks: Membranophones: a stretched skin/membrane vibrates
2 marks: Chordophones: a stretched string vibrates
2 marks: Aerophones: a vibrating column of air
4 marks: One example each (1 each): idiophone - ogene, ekwe, shekere, ichaka; membranophone - dundun, bata, kalangu; chordophone - goje, kuntigi, molo; aerophone - algaita, kakaki, oja
8 marks: Any four (2 each): sending messages/signals (talking drum); announcing the arrival of a king; summoning people to meetings; warning of danger; status symbols/royal regalia; ritual objects in shrines; marking time for work
questions.explanation: Idiophones (self-sounding: ogene), membranophones (skin: dundun), chordophones (string: goje), aerophones (air: algaita). Non-musical uses: signalling, royal regalia, summoning, ritual.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain how jazz developed among Black Americans. [6 marks]
(b) State four characteristics of jazz. [4 marks]
(c) Write short notes on any two of the following: (i) Louis Armstrong; (ii) Bob Marley; (iii) Miriam Makeba. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: Developed in the southern USA (New Orleans) around the late 19th/early 20th century from African-American work songs, spirituals, blues and ragtime blended with European harmony and brass band instruments (3 points x 2)
4 marks: Any four (1 each): improvisation; syncopation; swing rhythm; blue notes; call and response; use of brass, saxophone and rhythm section
5 marks: Louis Armstrong: American trumpeter and singer from New Orleans; major early jazz soloist, distinctive gravelly voice; e.g. "What a Wonderful World" (any 5 points)
5 marks: Bob Marley: Jamaican reggae singer and songwriter with The Wailers; Rastafarian themes, social justice and African unity; e.g. "No Woman, No Cry"; or Miriam Makeba: South African singer "Mama Africa", anti-apartheid voice, "Pata Pata" (any 5 points)
questions.explanation: Jazz grew in New Orleans from blues, spirituals, work songs and ragtime. It features improvisation, syncopation, swing and blue notes. Armstrong was a trumpet virtuoso; Marley spread reggae; Makeba was "Mama Africa".
